title.zh: 卷四十三 志第十三: 曆象志中
title.raw: 卷四十三 志第十三: 曆象志中 Volume 43 Treatises 13: Celestial Phenomena 2

sentences.zh: 曆象誌中 ○閏考

translations.literal: Treatise on Calendars and Celestial Signs, Part Two ○ Study of Intercalation
translations.idiomatic: Celestial Phenomena, Part Two — Intercalation

sentences.zh: 月度不足，是生朔虛；

translations.literal: When the measure of the month falls short, this gives rise to new-moon deficit;
translations.idiomatic: When a lunar month runs short of a full cycle, a "new-moon deficit" arises;

sentences.zh: 天行有餘，是為氣盈。

translations.literal: when heaven's motion has surplus, this constitutes qi surplus.
translations.idiomatic: when the sun's annual course runs long, the result is "qi surplus."

sentences.zh: 盈虛相懸，歲月乃牉，積牉而差，寒暑互易，百谷不成，庶政不明。

translations.literal: Surplus and deficit hang in opposition; only then do year and month come level; accumulated misleveling produces error, cold and heat exchange places, the hundred grains fail to ripen, and common administration lacks clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus and deficit pull against each other until year and month can be brought back into alignment; let misalignment accumulate and the seasons swap places, crops fail, and government loses its rhythm.

sentences.zh: 聖人驗以斗柄，準以歲星，爰立閏法，信治百官。

translations.literal: The sages verified by the Dipper's handle, took the Year Star as standard, thereupon established the intercalary rule, and reliably ordered the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The sages checked the seasons against the Dipper's handle and Jupiter's station, established intercalation on that basis, and thereby kept the civil calendar trustworthy for every office.

sentences.zh: 是故閏正而月正，月正而歲正。

translations.literal: Therefore when intercalation is correct the months are correct, and when the months are correct the year is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Correct intercalation makes the months right; correct months make the year right.

sentences.zh: 歲月既正，頒令考績，無有不時。

translations.literal: Once year and month are correct, edicts are issued and achievements examined, and none fail to be timely.
translations.idiomatic: With the calendar set right, orders go out and performance is reviewed on schedule.

sentences.zh: 國史正歲年以敘事，莫重於此。

translations.literal: The national chronicle sets the year aright to narrate affairs, and nothing is weightier than this.
translations.idiomatic: The court historians align the annual record to narrate events—nothing in statecraft weighs more.

sentences.zh: 遼始征歷梁、唐。

translations.literal: Liao at the outset sought calendars from Liang and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Liao turned to the Liang and Tang for calendrical systems.

sentences.zh: 入晉之後，奄有帝制，《乙未》、《大明》，曆法再變。

translations.literal: After entering Jin territory they suddenly possessed the imperial system; the 《Yiwei》 and 《Daming》 calendars saw the calendrical method change twice.
translations.idiomatic: Once they held the imperial mantle after entering Jin territory, they adopted the 《Yiwei》 and 《Daming》 systems in succession—two great calendar reforms.

sentences.zh: 穆宗應歷六年，周用顯德《欽天曆》；

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yingli under Emperor Muzong, Zhou employed the Xiande 《Qintian Calendar》;
translations.idiomatic: In Muzong's sixth Yingli year the Later Zhou used the Xiande-era 《Qintian Calendar》;

sentences.zh: 十年，宋用建隆《應天曆》。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Song employed the Jianlong 《Yingtian Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: in his tenth Yingli year the Song adopted the Jianlong 《Yingtian Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 景宗乾亨四年，宋用《乾元曆》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianheng under Emperor Jingzong, Song employed the 《Qianyuan Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzong's fourth Qianheng year the Song used the 《Qianyuan Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 聖宗統和十九年，宋用《儀天曆》；

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tonghe under Emperor Shengzong, Song employed the 《Yitian Calendar》;
translations.idiomatic: In Shengzong's nineteenth Tonghe year the Song used the 《Yitian Calendar》;

sentences.zh: 太平元年，宋用《崇天曆》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Song employed the 《Chongtian Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: in the first Taiping year the Song used the 《Chongtian Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 道宗清寧十年，宋用《明天曆》；

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qingning under Emperor Daozong, Song employed the 《Mingtian Calendar》;
translations.idiomatic: In Daozong's tenth Qingning year the Song used the 《Mingtian Calendar》;

sentences.zh: 大康元年，宋用《奉元曆》；

translations.literal: In the first year of Dakang, Song employed the 《Fengyuan Calendar》;
translations.idiomatic: in the first Dakang year the Song used the 《Fengyuan Calendar》;

sentences.zh: 大安七年，宋用《觀天曆》。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Da'an, Song employed the 《Guantian Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh Da'an year the Song used the 《Guantian Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 天祚皇帝乾統六年，宋用《紀元曆》。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiantong under Emperor Tianzuo, Song employed the 《Jiyuan Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianzuo's sixth Qiantong year the Song used the 《Jiyuan Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 五代歷三變，宋凡八變，遼終始再變。

translations.literal: Under the Five Dynasties the calendar changed three times; under Song it changed eight times in all; Liao from beginning to end changed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties saw three calendar reforms, the Song eight, and the Liao only two from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 曆法不齊，故定朔置閏，時有不同，覽者惑焉。

translations.literal: Calendrical methods were not uniform; therefore in fixing the new moon and placing intercalary months the times sometimes differed, and readers are perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Because their systems did not match, intercalary months and new-moon dates diverged, leaving readers baffled.

sentences.zh: 作《閏考》。

translations.literal: Therefore the 《Study of Intercalation》 was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this 《Study of Intercalation》.

translations.literal: (The text has tables on pages 540–564 of the book.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Tables occupy pages 540–564 of the printed edition.)〉
